items.author: Global Voices East Asia
items.title: Ex-lawmaker sentenced to 12.5 years in prison in closed-door trial in Macau
items.summary: Macau recorded its first conviction under the city’s national security law on November 6, 2026, sentencing 69-year-old former lawmaker Au Kam San to 12.5 years in prison. Observers call it an “unfair” “sham trial”

items.author: Jude Pierre Louis
items.title: From a quiet life to the terror of armed gangs: The story of Haiti’s Kenscoff district
items.summary: After the first of two deadly gang attacks this year, the Kenscoff community, like many other regions in the country, turned from peaceful living to being held to ransom.

items.author: Nshua Cali-Dibang
items.title: Big Tech, AI, and the quiet expansion of digital surveillance in Nigeria
items.summary: Systems designed to maximize commercial value from information can create incentives to collect more data than people reasonably expect or understand.

items.author: Sangita Swechcha
items.title: The dreamer who wants the world to read Nepali literature
items.summary: Rishi Ram Adhikari, founder of Kitab Yatra and Kitab Jatra Festival, discusses his mission to promote Nepali literature globally, build libraries and connect readers across borders through cultural exchange.

items.author: Carolina Pichardo
items.title: Beyond the beaches: The Dominican Republic and the global debate over deep-sea mining
items.summary: The DR wanted science to keep advancing and the International Seabed Authority to finish building the regulatory framework that the UN Convention had mandated it to develop.

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: How people in Montenegro are making their country cleaner
items.summary: While Montenegro works to align its waste management with EU directives, ordinary citizens are taking practical steps to improve the situation now.

items.author: Óscar Calles
items.title: Venezuela welcomes opposition leader María Corina Machado home
items.summary: Venezuela’s Nobel laureate María Corina Machado returned to Caracas in a massive celebration after months in hiding and exile, sparking deep hope and sharp questions about the country’s political future.

items.author: Global Voices
items.title: Global Voices condemns the attacks on Albanian fact-checking service Faktoje
items.summary: We stand in solidarity with Faktoje following a series of coordinated attacks that have weaponized its transparent financial data to undermine its vital work exposing misinformation around local protests.

items.author: Rebecca MacKinnon
items.title: What comes after networked authoritarianism?
items.summary: October’s spotlight on Big Tech and Authoritarianism explored a range of relationships between tech companies and political actors across the global majority.

items.author: Lina Ma
items.title: Unmarried Chinese women are rewriting the marriage script
items.summary: Some unmarried Chinese women are actively challenging the social stigma associated with being “leftover women” by questioning family pressure, sharing ways to escape it, or reframing the discussion altogether.
